name: LSM-775
summary: Psychedelic of the lysergamide class, the drug is less potent by weight than LSD. The drug is reported to produce mild, dreamy, sedating effects in contrast to LSD.

pharmacology.text: LSM-775 is a potent full agonist of the serotonin 5-HT1A receptor and a potent partial agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B, and 5-HT2C receptors. It does not produce the head-twitch response, a behavioral proxy of psychedelic effects, in rodents. However, LSM-775 can robustly increase head twitches if it is coadministered with the serotonin 5-HT1A receptor antagonist WAY-100635.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin receptor modulator; Serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist; Serotonergic psychedelic; Hallucinogen

uses.text: LSM-775 was first investigated in animal models in 1957, where it was observed to be "qualitatively similar to LSD" albeit with a significantly lower potency and "half the duration".
